props.title: Kicking and Screaming
props.initialSlug: Grads face post-college life with witty angst

sections.content: Noah Baumbach's directorial debut Kicking and Screaming perfectly captures post-college paralysis with razor-sharp dialogue and deadpan humor. Like Whit Stillman's Metropolitan (1990) and Richard Linklater's Slacker (1990), it crystallizes that specific moment when educated young adults face the void of real life. The film's protagonist Grover and his friends exist in a self-imposed limbo, clinging to campus life through endless pop culture references and pseudo-intellectual banter. Their witty deflections mask genuine terror about the future.

sections.content: This wave of 90s films about educated twenty-somethings reflected Generation X's particular brand of ironic detachment and analysis-paralysis. While Reality Bites (1994) took a more commercial approach with its MTV aesthetic and Winona Ryder star power, Baumbach's film stays defiantly small-scale and verbal. Its influence can be seen in later works like Garden State (2004) and Frances Ha (2012), which similarly explore arrested development among privileged, culturally literate young adults.

The film established many Baumbach signatures - the academic setting, literary references, characters who use intelligence as a defense mechanism. These themes would mature in later works like The Squid and the Whale (2005) and Marriage Story (2019). But there's a specific charm to how Kicking and Screaming captures that moment when cleverness and cultural knowledge stop being enough to coast on. SUBHEAD: The Post-College Film Genre

sections.content: While coming-of-age films typically focus on high school or early college, the post-graduation subgenre examines a specific type of privileged limbo. St. Elmo's Fire (1985) glamorized this transition period, but films like Tiny Furniture (2010) and The Graduate (1967) expose its existential dread. These characters have been trained to analyze and critique but struggle with actual living. Their education becomes both armor and prison.
